title: Arterial pressure monitoring systems
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Device-neutral educational specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.

parameters.name: Arterial pressure value
parameters.explanation: An arterial transducer provides a continuous pressure signal from which systolic, diastolic and mean pressures are displayed. Check levelling, zeroing and waveform quality if the values do not fit the patient.

parameters.name: Arterial waveform
parameters.explanation: Systolic upstroke, peak and diastolic decline reflect the pressure signal. A damped or resonant system can distort systolic and diastolic readings. Assess the patient and inspect the system when the trace changes.

parameters.name: Zero and levelling
parameters.explanation: Zeroing establishes the atmospheric reference. Levelling aligns the transducer with the intended anatomical reference and reduces hydrostatic error. Recheck the level after position changes under local policy.

safety_concepts.text: Keep all components of the pressure-monitoring system sterile (CDC Category IA).
Do not give dextrose-containing solutions or parenteral nutrition through the pressure-monitoring circuit (CDC IA).
Scrub the diaphragm with an appropriate antiseptic before accessing the system through a diaphragm (CDC IA).
Prefer a closed continuous-flush system and minimise manipulations and entries (CDC Category II).

monitoring_concepts.text: Arterial pressure and waveform, heart rate, limb perfusion, insertion site, flush system, alarms and line days.

escalation_concepts.text: Escalate immediately for bleeding or disconnection (apply pressure and call for help), a cold, pale or painful limb, a lost or implausible waveform that cannot be corrected, signs of infection or suspected injection into the line.
